scope: Two recorded real model stories, fresh synthetic authority journeys and live platform photographs. No browser/player data. Path checks are not rendered play or pacing evidence.

actions.text:
The gray-haired man looks up. “Call me Zhou. I repair watches here. You must be here for the letter?”
Take the key; bring it back when you’re done.
He hands it to you.
You lift the bolt on the workshop side. The courtyard gate opens, making a shortcut home.
The key turns and the compartment opens. Inside is a sealed letter addressed to your family.
You put away the letter without opening it. The filing slip points to the street records your family asked about; the shop ledger can help you locate them.

Filing slip: Stamped with 'Archival Dept.'; Folded twice with a thin twine tie.
Sidewalk slabs were leveled and reset: Stamped with 'Archival Dept.'; Folded twice with a thin twine tie
Fire hydrants were pressure-tested and certified: Faded ink notation on upper edge; Folded twice with a thin twine tie
Streetlamp bulbs were replaced citywide: Stamped with 'Archival Dept.'; Sealed with a wax emblem imprint
Both details match. The packet is on the old paper shelf in the cellar.
You borrow the trolley, leaving its parking bay empty.
You wheel the crates into the clear space by the wall, revealing the steps down.
Two entries were filed together: “Sidewalk slabs were leveled and reset” and “Complaints filed about uneven sidewalk hazards”. This filing slip does not explain their order.
You pack the papers to bring home with the sealed letter. The original is no longer on the shelf.
The archive is through the cellar’s east doorway. Look for the index, work log and sorting table inside.A movable storage rack blocks the work index; an empty space beside it lets you slide it aside.
The rack slides aside. You can now reach the work index.
You take the insert. Spread it on the table to examine it, or return it to its shelf.

You spread out the insert and compare its lines.
“Complaints filed about uneven sidewalk hazards” happened before “City council approved funds for sidewalk repairs”.
Loan slip: the work log is at the photo studio viewing table. Read it there, then bring your notes back to compare.

“City council approved funds for sidewalk repairs” happened before “Contractors began leveling and resetting slabs”.
“Contractors began leveling and resetting slabs” happened before “Sidewalk slabs were leveled and reset”.
The two sources agree: “Complaints filed about uneven sidewalk hazards” happened before “Sidewalk slabs were leveled and reset”.
The trolley is back in its place.
You copy the verified account into the record book for later visitors. The original papers and sealed letter stay where you chose to keep them.
Your exploration idea is saved. You can keep exploring while the new area is prepared.
The darkroom door can now be opened.
The photograph shows a close-up of a sidewalk with clearly visible leveled and reset concrete slabs.
You tuck the completed street photograph into your bag.

You return the key. The watchmaker smiles.
You kept your word. Thank you.
You leave the old street and deliver the sealed letter to your family.
